query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor boron (B) dopant (≤0.5 at%) into a eutectic high-entropy alloy during casting will refine the lamellar microstructure and reinforce grain boundaries in a manner that simultaneously increases strength and enhances ductility relative to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., CoCrFeNiNb-based or similar), prior to boron addition and standard solution heat treatment.
generation.intervention: Incorporate up to 0.5 at% boron into the melt prior to solidification handling under otherwise equivalent casting and processing conditions.
generation.conditions: Alloy processed by standard vacuum induction melting, followed by a typical solutionizing treatment at ~1100–1200 °C, and subsequently air-cooled or water-quenched.
generation.structural_mediator: Refined lamellar microstructure and strengthened grain boundaries via boron segregation and/or boride formation at interfaces, which collectively impede dislocation motion while promoting controlled plastic flow.
generation.mechanism: Boron acts as a surfactant at grain boundaries and may generate boron-rich interfacial phases that both inhibit dislocation movement (increasing strength) and stabilize local plasticity pathways (improving ductility).
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength increases by around 15–20% (versus baseline) while uniform elongation is retained or increased by ~5–10%.
generation.baseline: Equivalent eutectic high-entropy alloy without boron addition, similarly cast and thermally treated.
generation.boundary: Mechanisms may depend on the specific alloy chemistry and processing route; excessive boron or differing heat treatments could lead to coarse boride formation that diminishes ductility.
generation.uncertainty: Exact compositional limits for boron, the reproducibility of lamellar refinement, and the interplay of second-phase particles are not fully established and require systematic study.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of eutectic high-entropy alloy samples under identical casting and thermal histories: one set with ~0.5 at% B and one set without B. Characterize the microstructure via scanning/transmission electron microscopy, then perform tensile tests and fractographic analysis to measure changes in yield strength and ductility.
measurements: Lamellar spacing and grain size via SEM/TEM imaging
Elemental distribution at grain boundaries (EDS or atom probe tomography)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If boron addition does not refine the lamellae or fails to increase yield strength and/or ductility relative to the boron-free baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
